- Register: "PULS ELECTRONIK SISTEMLERI"
- Document: "PULS ELECTRONIK SISTEMLERI MAK. SAN. IÇ VE DIŞ TIC. LTD. ŞTI."

The document version is the register value plus a trade-name/legal-suffix expansion: "MAK. SAN. IÇ VE DIŞ TIC. LTD. ŞTI." which is Turkish for "Makine Sanayi İç ve Dış Ticaret Limited Şirketi" (Machine Manufacturing, Domestic and Foreign Trade Limited Company). This is a legal-suffix / fuller legal-form expansion of the same company. The core name "PULS ELECTRONIK SISTEMLERI" matches exactly.

Per rules: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." So this is same-entity. The best value — the fused record should carry... For same-entity cases, which value? The rule says for "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." For name same-entity, the document is the legal instrument, and the document has the fuller, more complete legal name. Generally best practice for fusion: prefer the more complete legal name from the certificate document since it's the legal instrument. The rules only explicitly say "best_value from the register" for document-noise, and "register's canonical form" for number formats. For same-entity names with legal-suffix drift, the document's fuller form is arguably better since the certificate is the legal instrument. The document value contains the register value entirely, so it's a superset — the more complete legal name.

I'll go with same-entity, best_value = the document's fuller legal name, since it's a superset and the certificate is the legal instrument. Verdict: "same-entity".
